- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.17) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.22) in recent days, model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price is trending up.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days); cap forecast at 1.5x recent peak unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3-5 consecutive days show price moving away from 80–85 range, model tends to overcorrect; dampen forecast toward historical mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overpredicts late-period (last 10–15 days) prices; reduce forecast tail end by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- If sentiment turns positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-estimate from midpoint onward with sentiment-weighted drift.
